column4: statement_en
The product unit is a versioned Workflow Template with fixed inputs, outputs, risks, pricing and tests. The router selects an approved template; it never composes a free chain per request.
All model and tool calls are backend-to-backend behind an API gateway. No provider keys in any browser.
tenant_id is derived from the authenticated identity and enforced in IAM, DB, object storage, queues and RAG.
The professional output is a typed Finding bound to evidence and to a reviewer decision.
Two independent risk axes: Action Risk R0-R4 (authority to act) and Professional Consequence P0-P3 (impact of error).
column9: P3 requires specialist; R4 requires delegation

column4: A reviewer decision binds to an artifact version and its SHA-256 digest; any change restarts the review cycle.
Work never starts from a payment redirect. Activation requires a verified signed webhook plus server-side fetch, under idempotency.
A database row never proves execution. READY requires build reference, passed test, evidence link and a qualified approver.
No embedding and no quotation of a source before its usage right is recorded as ALLOWED.
AI proposes; professional approval is given by a named qualified human within a defined scope.
Launch scope is a single-tenant owned operation with tenant-aware primitives retained for future commerce.
column9: single-tenant launch with enforced tenant context

column4: White-label, external tenants and subscription sales are explicitly deferred out of launch scope.
column9: owner authorization required before any work

column4: Control path is Admin Console -> authenticated Platform API -> policy/approval -> workflow/agent runtime. Never browser-to-agent and never browser-to-database.
A release gate record must carry logs, test artifacts, owner, environment, timestamp and deployment SHA.
The source describes architecture, not a verified running implementation; a runtime inventory with live integration tests is required before any readiness claim.
column9: runtime inventory + deploy SHA + test output

column4: Saudi authority integrations require formal provider agreements, credentials and sandbox verification before being presented as available.
Control status words DEFINED and DESIGNED are documentation states only and must never be rendered as READY.
Any READY claim without attached evidence must be removed from all artifacts.
Tenant isolation is enforced by RLS, partitioning, object key prefixes, queue scoping and vector filters, with tenant derived from identity.
Organization entity: org_id, legal_name, commercial_id, status; exactly one contractual owner; lifecycle lead->contract->active->suspended->terminated.
Tenant entity: tenant_id, org_id, region, plan_id; tenant context immutable; default deny; lifecycle provision->active->archive.
Workspace entity: workspace_id, tenant_id, brand_id; multiple workspaces per organization when required.
Membership entity with RBAC plus ABAC and SSO/MFA; authority expressed as JWT scopes plus a policy service.
Project entity: project_id, tenant_id, owner_id; moving files between organizations without approval is prohibited.
Ten access surfaces with distinct identity and access boundaries: public, individuals, business, engineer, reviewer, pmo, contractor, support, control, api.

Ten platform roles with explicit allow, data scope, deny, authentication strength and review cadence: PLATFORM_OWNER, TENANT_ADMIN, PROJECT_MANAGER, EXECUTION_ENGINEER, QUALIFIED_REVIEWER, PMO_CONTROLLER, FINANCE, SUPPORT_L2, API_CLIENT, AUDITOR.
IAM provides OIDC, MFA, step-up authentication, JIT elevation and audited break-glass with expiry.
Secrets live in a vault with rotation; no secrets in prompts, logs or client bundles.
File security: pre-signed upload, size and type limits, AV scan, sandboxed parsing, quarantine on detection.
Encryption in transit and at rest, with managed keys and encrypted backups.
Audit and evidence stores are append-only or WORM and record before/after values, actor, time and correlation id.
LLM and tool safety: tool allowlist, least privilege, prompt-injection defences and egress control.
Prompt injection and tool exfiltration protections require an adversarial red-team suite covering tool allowlist, egress policy and input trust labels.
PDPL lawful basis: documented purpose, lawful basis, consent where required and privacy notice, recorded in a RoPA.
Data subject rights: access, correction, destruction and withdrawal of consent, with identity verification and SLA.
Retention schedules with legal hold and verified deletion.
Breach process: triage, contain, assess and notify, with a 72-hour regulator trigger where applicable.
Processor governance: DPA, subprocessor register, due diligence and transfer assessment.
Payment security: hosted or tokenized capture, webhook signature verification, idempotency and reconciliation.
Electronic signature controls: identity, intent, hash binding, timestamp, certificate and revocation.
Availability controls: backups, disaster recovery, defined RTO and RPO, queue durability and circuit breakers.
No PAN or CVV is ever stored; PCI scope is explicitly bounded.

Twenty core entities with defined keys, purpose, source, retention and integrity control: Tenant, User, Project, WorkflowTemplate, WorkflowRun, Task, Artifact, Finding, Evidence, Citation, Reviewer, Eligibility, Assignment, ReviewDecision, Quote, Payment, Delivery, Consent, AuditEvent, EvaluationRun.
projects: required id, tenant_id, customer_id, status, version; UNIQUE (tenant_id, id); indexes on tenant_id and status.
workflow_runs: UNIQUE (tenant_id, idempotency_key); indexes on project_id, status, created_at.
agent_executions: UNIQUE (run_id, step_id, attempt); prompts redacted at rest.
evidence_assets: UNIQUE (tenant_id, id); AV scan and immutable sha256 required.
review_decisions: UNIQUE (artifact_id, review_version); append-only.
boq_items: UNIQUE (estimate_id, line_no); unit and source references mandatory; versioned snapshots.
usage_ledger: execution_id UNIQUE; exactly-once posting.
outbox_events: event_id UNIQUE; transactional outbox with status and next_attempt_at.
idempotency_keys: UNIQUE (tenant_id, key); conflict on request-hash mismatch; TTL per operation.

Workflow state machine with explicit DRAFT, QUOTED, AWAITING_PAYMENT, PAYMENT_VERIFIED, QUEUED, RUNNING, AWAITING_INFORMATION, AWAITING_REVIEW, AWAITING_SECOND_REVIEW, AWAITING_CLIENT_DECISION, DELIVERED, ARCHIVED, FAILED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED, SUSPENDED and PARTIALLY_COMPLETED states.
Every run pins the exact workflow template version it started on; publishing a new version never migrates in-flight runs.
Durable orchestration survives worker restart with no lost jobs.
Side effects are idempotent: repeating an idempotency key never duplicates a charge or an action.
Review sub-state machine: OFFERED, ACCEPTED, IN_REVIEW, DECIDED, NEEDS_INFORMATION, EXPIRED with COI and hash-pinning controls.
Delivery sub-state machine: CANDIDATE, LOCKED, SIGNED, RELEASED, INVALIDATED, where a digest change forces INVALIDATED.

Eight workflow templates with version, sector, scope, capability list, R/P rating, review requirement, pricing id and test suite id: WF-VILLA-REVIEW 1.0.0, WF-BIM-COORD 0.9.0, WF-QTO 0.9.0, WF-SITE-REPORT 0.9.0, WF-MEP-REVIEW 0.8.0, WF-INFRA-REVIEW 0.8.0, WF-PAYMENT 1.0.0, WF-REVIEW-DELIVERY 1.0.0.

WF-VILLA-REVIEW golden path has ten ordered stages with transition conditions, failure states and human gates: Intake, Routing, Quote and payment, File intelligence, Compliance, Architecture draft, Quality gate, Reviewer assignment, Finding review, Lock/sign/deliver.
Run orchestration manages tasks, deadlines, dependencies, waits and retries under a state machine, and halts when idempotency cannot be guaranteed or the retry budget is exceeded.
The router selects an approved template version by policy and registry; absence of a match yields manual triage, never an invented path. Retired versions and invalid schemas are rejected.

Nineteen product API operations with purpose, OAuth scope, idempotency or concurrency control, emitted event and response codes, spanning projects, requests, uploads, quotes, payments, webhooks, workflow-runs, findings, reviews, deliveries and public verification.
Ten typed API contracts API-01..API-10 with named request and response schemas, scopes, retry semantics, status codes, events and security invariants.
Cross-tenant existence must never be revealed; unauthorized reads return a response that leaks no metadata.
A common event envelope carries eventId, eventType, schemaVersion, tenantId, correlationId, causationId, occurredAt in UTC and payload.
Eight versioned domain events EV-01..EV-08 with aggregate, required payload fields, producer, consumer, ordering key, at-least-once delivery and a validation rule.
POST /v1/ai/execute accepts tenant_id, project_id, task_type, risk, modality, input_refs, budget and idempotency_key; tenant is always server-derived and a client-supplied tenant_id is never trusted.
Execution read API returns state, spans, costs, model versions and evidence refs under role scoping; the SSE event stream carries progress and partial artifacts and never secrets or PII.
Gateway emits ai.execution.completed and ai.execution.failed v1 events, at-least-once, with consumer-side dedupe, DLQ and redaction.

Eight operations admin API surface for health, agent deployments, connector registration and probe, execution retry, model policy release, audit search and scan sessions, each with scope, idempotency requirement and emitted event.
A private AI gateway provides a single /v1/ai/execute entry with a typed task envelope and SSE streaming, behind service OIDC auth, tenant and project RBAC, WAF and idempotency.
column9: p95 gateway overhead measured against a stated target

column4: A preflight policy engine classifies data, geography, consent, allowed tools and task risk, fails closed, and logs 100 percent of policy decisions.
A capability registry selects eligible models by verified capability, modality, Arabic support, context window and availability, allowlisted by data classification.

An adaptive router is quality-first for high-risk tasks and least-cost within a validated tier for routine tasks; deterministic rules come first and a contextual bandit is permitted only after evaluation.
Provider adapters normalize contracts across providers with secrets in a vault, an egress allowlist and no keys in the browser; timeouts, retries and circuit breakers are mandatory.
A fallback controller stays within the approved region and classification and preserves quality equivalence; it never silently downgrades critical engineering verification.
A context compiler builds task-scoped context with citations, semantic de-duplication and tenant-scoped ACL-filtered retrieval, and reports tokens saved against a baseline.
Prompt caching uses stable prefixes where supported and is isolated by tenant, classification and model version with no cross-tenant leakage.
A budget controller enforces per-task, per-tenant daily and monthly token and SAR caps with a preflight estimate, hard stop and approval thresholds.
An output validator enforces JSON schema, source provenance and deterministic math and CAD checks, and requires human approval for safety-critical conclusions.
OpenTelemetry tracing plus a usage ledger record every span, token count, cost, latency and error, with PII scrubbing and scoped retention, and 100 percent of billable usage recorded.
An admin control plane holds versioned policies with staged rollout, rollback and approvals, and four-eyes control for production secrets and policies.

Model registry fields: model_id, provider and region, capabilities, data_policy, per-task quality_score, p50/p95 latency, cost in/out per million tokens, limits, health and circuit state, release_status. A global generic quality score is prohibited.

Eight routing policies by task class with candidate tier, strategy, quality check, fallback rule and cost control: OCR/extraction, routine support, architectural reasoning, SBC compliance, BOQ/costing, LiDAR geometry, live scan narration, safety/structural.
No LLM is used for measurement ground truth; LiDAR and CAD geometry are produced by deterministic tools and geometry is transmitted instead of video.
For safety and structural tasks the LLM assists only; a licensed reviewer approves and the path fails closed.
Provider topology is multi-provider through an independent gateway; hard lock-in to a single aggregator is rejected.
The initial model set is chosen by benchmarking two premium reasoning, two fast and two vision candidates; assuming a model is best without evaluation is rejected.
Data privacy follows approved geography and vendor retention per classification; assuming any gateway is Saudi-resident is rejected.
Nine model SLA policy controls with metric, fallback, proof and owner: quality tier, residency and privacy, budget, efficiency, reliability, load, correctness, version control.

Ten agent runtime contract areas RT-01..RT-10 with fields, invariants and failure actions: execution identity, agent definition, context package, model routing, execution controls, result envelope, evidence and audit, usage ledger, HITL escalation, failure taxonomy.
A context package never mixes projects or tenants and carries signed references under least privilege.
Agent versions are pinned and immutable; unregistered tools are blocked at dispatch.
The result envelope is JSON-schema validated and fails closed on invalid output.
A failure taxonomy with errorCode, retryable, providerFailure and partialArtifacts drives a circuit breaker and dead-letter queue; silent success is prohibited.

Five agent lifecycle objects with mandatory fields, release gate, rollback rule and notes: AgentDefinition, AgentVersion, AgentDeployment, AgentRun, AgentOutput. Arbitrary dynamic tools are prohibited and published versions are immutable.
Registry capability entries are not equivalent to deployable agent versions; immutable versions with staged rollout are required.

Forty-four agent capabilities across control, governance, documents, studies, planning, sustainability, compliance, design disciplines, infrastructure, geotechnical, data, BIM, cost, execution, procurement, site, safety, quality, vision, handover, operations, finance, FinOps, review, evaluation and eight PMO capabilities; each with inputs, outputs, tools, knowledge, R rating, P rating, human gate, stop conditions, workflows, KPIs and owner.
column9: capability registry completeness + per-capability stop-condition test

column4: Eight PMO capabilities PMO-01..PMO-08 with deep role, inputs, outputs, P rating, human approver, stop conditions, KPIs and owner.
Agent catalog metadata: versioned SKU, capabilities with input and output schemas, bundles, dependencies, allowed models, human gate, customization, limits and immediate suspend or revoke.
Agent studio stages: choose, configure, knowledge, branding, sandbox, publish, operate, rollback, each with platform validation, API, security policy and output.

Ten RAG collections with users, metadata, strategy, owner, refresh cadence and risk rating: RAG-SBC, RAG-BALADY, RAG-SCE, RAG-PROJECT, RAG-CLIENT, RAG-CONTRACT, RAG-PRICES, RAG-QA-HSE, RAG-OEM, RAG-GOLDEN.
SRC-SBC-2024 rights for licence, storage, embedding, quotation and redistribution are all UNKNOWN; the source decision is BLOCK until ALLOWED.

A source rights register records owner, link or contract, type, licence, storage right, embedding right, quotation right, redistribution right, reviewer, last review date and decision for every corpus.
Project knowledge is indexed per project with tenant, project, ACL, revision, hash and classification metadata and never crosses tenants.
Every normative citation includes the code edition and an applicability statement.
Compliance capability determines applicable code editions and jurisdiction and converts permitted text into rules and cited findings; it halts on UNKNOWN rights, unknown edition or conflict.
The golden evaluation collection is evaluation-only with consent, usage right, de-identification, labels and split, under leakage control.

The Finding schema has twenty-one fields with type and obligation, including finding_id, tenant_id, workflow id and version, project and artifact version, discipline, finding_type, severity, action_risk, professional_consequence, statement, evidence array, citations array, confidence, recommended_action, status, created_by, reviewer_decision, reason_code, reviewer_comment, reviewed_hash and decision_signature_ref.
Every finding carries mandatory evidence locators: artifact, page, grid, GUID and hash.
Machine confidence is a calibrated score and is never treated as an approval.

Reviewer registry has fifteen field groups with classification, verification method, renewal cadence and obligation: identity, identity status, SCE reference, membership status and expiry, discipline, professional scope, experience evidence, platform assessment, agreement status, COI declarations, availability, rate card, performance metrics, approval status and security.

Eight eligibility codes with discipline, conditions, scope, prohibitions, second-review trigger and validity: ARCH-RES-VILLA, STRUCT-LOWRISE, ELEC-BUILDING, MECH-HVAC, FIRE-REVIEW, BIM-COORD, QS-QTO, CIVIL-INFRA.
Reviewer assignment has ten ordered stages: task profile, hard filters, COI check, independence check, ranking, offer, accept and declare, artifact lock, SLA handling and quality follow-up.
Hard filters are non-overridable: verified identity, valid membership, eligibility, signed agreement, MFA and capacity; each failure is a documented exclusion.
Independence is enforced: the producer of an output never reviews it, and four-eyes separation applies.
Ranking weights are discipline 30 percent, eligibility 20 percent, quality 15 percent, availability 15 percent, sector 10 percent and language or location 10 percent, approved per workflow.
No automated penalty is applied to a reviewer without human review.
Delivery has ten ordered steps: prepare candidate, quality gate, lock, assign, decide findings, sign decision, commercial gate, release, verify and change-after-sign.
Release requires a paid milestone or a contractual authorization recorded as payment evidence.
A limited public verification page exposes the digest and status and supports revocation.
Any change after signature produces a new version and digest and re-enters review; silent replacement is prohibited.
The delivery package is generated from approved findings with a manifest, digest, certificate and QR, and never signs on behalf of an engineer.

The pricing engine has twelve components with formula, source and control: scope base, size, complexity, AI inference, document AI, engineering tools, reviewer, PMO, risk reserve, payment fees, target margin and VAT.
Every cost rate in the quote calculator is zero except VAT; actual contract values must be entered before any commercial quotation.

Quote computation chain: size cost, AI cost, tool cost, direct reviewer fee, PMO cost, direct cost, reserve, revenue share, pre-VAT price by gross-up, final reviewer payout, VAT amount, total, expected profit and margin percentage, with a CHECK INPUTS guard when the gross-up denominator is non-positive.
Pricing is reproducible: identical input snapshots must produce an identical quote.
A quote records inputs, rate snapshots and expiry and is locked on acceptance.
Payment lifecycle states INITIATED, AUTHORIZED, PAID, FAILED, EXPIRED, REFUNDED and CHARGEBACK are audited; a redirect never opens the service.
Payment handling is idempotent: the same provider event is applied exactly once.

Candidate payment and invoicing integrations with their controls: Moyasar, Geidea, Tamara BNPL, bank transfer with virtual IBAN reconciliation and ZATCA Fatoorah e-invoicing. A transfer screenshot never opens a milestone.
ZATCA e-invoicing onboarding requires EGS registration, certificates, secrets and tests before production invoicing.
AI usage is attributed to tenant and workflow across tokens, OCR, vision, BIM and storage, and runaway loops are prevented.
Usage metering must reconcile against provider billing with ledger idempotency and daily reconciliation.

Nine observability dashboards with signals, dimensions, alert trigger examples and actions: golden signals, capacity, model quality, cost, reliability, retrieval, scan ingestion, privacy and trace drilldown.
A single trace links trace_id to task, agent, model, tool, evidence and review; missing linkage is an instrumentation defect.

Seven SRE runbooks with detection, immediate response and recovery evidence: 429 throttling, provider outage, high spend, latency spike, bad-answer regression, cross-tenant exposure and scan upload failure.

Seven support operations scenarios with trigger, first response, safe action, escalation, evidence and target: model 429, workflow stuck, API failure, bad engineering result, data exposure, low LiDAR confidence and cost spike.
Twelve KPIs with target, unit, source and action, where current values may only be populated from documented operational sources and never from placeholder numbers.

Eleven evaluation and learning metrics with definition, segmentation, threshold, cadence, owner and use, including finding precision, finding recall, citation validity, reviewer override, inter-reviewer agreement, escalation accuracy, workflow failure, time to signed delivery, cost per workflow, gross margin and cross-tenant incidents.
A ten-stage learning cycle: capture, review, label, sample, measure, segment, investigate, improve, validate, release and monitor.

Seven capture modes with entry surface, device capability, captured payload, UX states, fallback and verification: photo, guided video, live analysis, LiDAR RoomPlan, manual measures, evidence package and privacy.
Live analysis samples frames and events and must not send every frame to a model; it carries a latency and cost budget.

Eight scan API operations and events with request fields, response, auth, idempotency and validation: start capture, upload chunk, commit evidence, analysis request, progress stream, capture quality event, evidence ready event and agent run completed event.
LiDAR output is not a certified engineering survey; confidence thresholds and mandatory human validation are required, evidenced by a device field validation report.
Camera permissions and PDPL handling require consent, deletion, redaction and a DPA as a P0 release blocker.
Scan engineering modes define entry point, processing, output, constraint and owner, and state that no continuous raw stream is sent by default and the result is not a certified survey.

Sixteen admin capabilities with role, approval requirement, API, audit flag, safety boundary and launch priority, spanning dashboard, tenants, agents, models, integrations, workflows, execution, knowledge, support, security, billing, scan and commerce.
An admin RBAC matrix for nine staff roles across eight sensitive actions: view health, view customer PII, edit agent, edit API, change model, retry jobs, billing and approve release.
Admin operations currently lack complete authorization and audit contracts; RBAC plus ABAC with dual control and append-only audit is required.
Connector lifecycle has six stages with contract, security, observability and verification: register, authenticate, validate, execute, fail and retire.
Connector validation enforces OpenAPI schema checking, a test endpoint, quota, SSRF protection and TLS.
Eight admin control areas mapping frontend action to backend authority, agent-layer relation, audit and security requirement and acceptance criterion.
Break-glass staff role elevation expires automatically and is dual-approved.

Fifteen Saudi integration targets with access reality, connection plan, users, link and status: Nafath, SCE, Balady Open Data, Balady Transactions, SBC 2024, Etimad API portal, ZATCA Fatoorah, SPL National Address, GEOSA, Open Data Saudi, NCA, SDAIA PDPL, SAMA PSP list, Saber and Salamah.
SCE membership verification has no proven public API; an official channel or documented manual review is required and scraping is prohibited.
Nafath integration is conditional on enterprise onboarding and is not a public API; OTP and MFA serve as the interim path.
Saudi integrations must not be presumed available; credential, licensing and contract verification is required per provider with provider sandbox success as evidence.

Twenty-nine engineering tool candidates with category, use, consuming agents, integration mode, controls, official link and adoption decision ranging from Production to Specialist, Evaluate, Option and Enterprise.

Thirteen acceptance tests AT-WF-001, AT-WF-002, AT-SEC-001, AT-REV-001, AT-REV-002, AT-DEL-001, AT-PAY-001, AT-PAY-002, AT-RAG-001, AT-PRIV-001, AT-EVAL-001, AT-PRICE-001 and AT-FILE-001, each with scenario, expected result, environment and owner, all currently PENDING.
Sixteen controls CTRL-001..CTRL-016 with priority, required evidence, test id and owner.
An evaluation regression gate blocks release when a candidate falls below threshold.
Seven model evaluation dimensions with test method, release threshold and evidence: engineering correctness, grounding, Arabic quality, latency, reliability, cost and privacy, all NOT TESTED.
Ten traceability requirements REQ-01..REQ-10 each bound to an API reference, event reference, acceptance test, owner, evidence state and required proof; the default evidence state is Not verified.
Ten production readiness gates G-01..G-10 with verification, pass criterion, owner, required evidence and a Block release decision, all Open.
A production evidence ledger with twelve gate rows G01..G12, each requiring test or proof, environment, owner, evidence URL, execution time and result, all currently NOT RUN.
Twelve go-live gates G01..G12 with requirement, test evidence, responsible owner, priority and release-blocker flag; eleven are P0 blockers and all are UNVERIFIED.

Ten gateway release gates G01..G10 covering provider DPA and residency, Arabic and SBC benchmarks, load and soak, chaos, tenant isolation including RAG cache traces and logs, cost ledger reconciliation, human approval, rollback and secret rotation, scan privacy and DPIA, and tested dashboards and runbooks, all NOT VERIFIED.
Eight executive cockpit controls are UNVERIFIED and release approval is BLOCKED until evidence plus accountable sign-off exists.

Six service catalog entries with inputs, workflow, accountable role, output acceptance and guardrail: architecture villa concept, document compliance review, BOQ extraction, cost estimate, field evidence package and cross-discipline clash review.
No licensed approval is ever issued by AI; every regulated output requires an accountable human role.
WF-BIM-COORD covers federation, IDS and clash detection with BCF, requiring BIM coordinator plus discipline owner review.
WF-QTO produces traceable quantities under LOD constraints with QS or cost manager review.
WF-MEP-REVIEW performs separated and coordinated MEP review with a reviewer per discipline.
WF-INFRA-REVIEW covers roads, networks, levels and connection points with civil, survey and geotechnical review.
WF-SITE-REPORT converts site evidence into a report and candidate progress under site engineer review.
Five pricing scenarios SCN-01..SCN-05 describing capability counts, review needs, complexity drivers, pricing method and launch sequencing, with capability count explicitly not a pricing unit.

A seven-stage product roadmap from product and risk fixing through foundation, villa MVP, controlled pilot, BIM/QTO/MEP, PMO and enterprise, to site, infrastructure and handover, each with duration, owners, evidence and a decision gate.

Eight commerce capabilities COM-01..COM-08 covering B2C and B2B, agent-as-a-service, private workspace, white-label, hosted and embedded delivery, sales-assisted enterprise, usage metering and data ownership with export, all DESIGN ONLY.
Five white-label delivery modes with entry point, identity, branding, features and guardrails: hosted, custom domain, embedded widget, API-only and enterprise private.
Six billing SKUs with billing unit, included entitlement, overage, controls, lifecycle and commercial caveat; prices are explicitly to be set commercially.
Nine B2B API operations for organizations, quotes, subscriptions, agent catalog, agent bundles, tenant agents, branding, usage and runs, with error cases, access control and SLO evidence.
Ten requirement deltas D01..D10 identifying B2B gaps against prior coverage with owner, reference sheet, priority and validation method.
Multi-tenant monetization is deferred for launch; single-tenant first with enforced tenant context.
Whether a deployed Sketch Design runtime, VPS, integrations and secrets currently exist cannot be established from the source; the source itself states the runtime environment was not accessed.
Numeric targets for finding precision, finding recall, citation validity, workflow failure rate, time to signed delivery and cost per workflow are TBD and may only be set from a real baseline.

All commercial rates, provider token rates, tool rates, reviewer rates, PMO rates, risk reserve, PSP fees and target margin are zero or unset in the source and must be supplied from executed contracts.
The source carries conflicting version and date markers: cover states v6.0 dated 04 October 2026 while rows and sheets reference v7, v8, v9, v10 and v11 content in one artifact.

Two different execution plans coexist: the product roadmap on sheet 29 sequences villa MVP before platform expansion, while the v10 release plan on sheet 67 sequences admin, agent lifecycle, connector vault and model routing first.
The visual identity is a temporary wordmark embedded in the workbook and must be replaced by the official logo when supplied.
Enterprise reliability of a free or local model baseline is unproven; paid and direct providers must be benchmarked before reliance.
